## Summary

Answered whether moving to Rust would be a disadvantage or a good-to-have, and in the process found a caveat that weakens the escape hatch this session has been recommending. Logged it as a note. The framing given: a full rewrite is an active disadvantage for reasons specific to this repo rather than generic rewrite cost, chiefly that it destroys the one-artifact distribution property the Homebrew decision was explicitly built on, since the formula sources the immutable npm tarball precisely because the bundle has zero runtime deps and brew can therefore never drift from npm; it also ends the JS library surface including the browser bundle, and it taxes every future feature because agent sessions write this codebase and are weaker in Rust. Rust is a genuine good-to-have only as a held option, and the important point is that the option can be held without paying for it, since the architecture already carries the seam. The caveat found: speed-2 D1 rejected a second hand-written hook implementation for two-sources-of-truth reasons, and a native hook binary is structurally that same rejected option, because it must re-implement the argv recognition and cannot fall through to the full CLI without paying the Node boot it exists to avoid. The hook-path carve-out is therefore not the cheap few-hundred-line move it appears to be, and anyone acting on it must read speed-2 D1 first. Both the artifact and the typescript-7 decision present that carve-out as a graceful downgrade, so the note records that the framing understates its cost.
